# A tree-store menu shows records the store's filters hide

## Context

Found while shaping #21061: permission-driven navigation filters one `Neo.data.TreeStore` and lets a `Neo.menu.List` cascade render it. The menu ignores the filter.

Reproducer (`test/playwright/unit/menu/ListTreeStore.spec.mjs` fixture: `file` → (`file-new` → `file-new-f`, `file-open`), `edit` → `edit-copy`, `about`), red on `dev` @ fbb9c4da19:

- **Filter set before the menus exist.** `{property: 'text', value: 'Copy'}` keeps `edit` and `edit-copy` only, yet the root menu lists `file, edit, about`.
- **Filter changed while the menus exist.** `{property: 'text', operator: 'included', value: ['New', 'Copy']}` leaves the root at `file, edit, about` and the `file` level at `file-new, file-open`.

Note for readers: TreeStore filtering is ancestor-aware. A group that matches a filter itself keeps its whole subtree, so a filter like `id !== 'file-open'` keeps `file-open` because `file` matched. That is intended tree semantics, not this bug. (This body's first version cited exactly that case as a symptom; corrected.)

## The Problem

A menu level never consults the tree store's filter mask:

1. `syncLevelRecords()` fills a level from `TreeStore#getChildren()` (`src/menu/List.mjs:985-992`), which reads the Structural Layer and is documented as independent of filtering (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:750-752`).
2. A level subscribes to the source store's `mutate`, `recordChange` and `sort` (`src/menu/List.mjs:759-764`), not `filter`, so a filter applied after the menu exists never reaches it.
3. `onSourceStoreMutate()` (`src/menu/List.mjs:926-943`) adds every record that belongs to the level, including ones the active filter hides.

Any app that narrows a menu by data (permissions, feature flags, a search box over a command menu) shows items the store says are gone.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: #17839, which introduced tree-store menus, states in its Out of Scope that the menu adopts "`TreeStore` for its **structural** half (`#childrenMap`, ancestor-aware filtering)", and `menu.List#sourceStore` documents "The tree store is the single source of truth and is shared by every level of the cascade" (`src/menu/List.mjs:192-199`). The levels read the structure but not the filter, so the intent never reached them.

`TreeStore#getChildren()`'s filter independence is its own contract for structural reads (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:740-766`) and stays unchanged; the mask applies at the level. #17839's rejected alternative (each level rendering a filtered subset of the shared store, unsafe for `list.Base` index math) is not reopened: each level keeps its own flat store and only adopts the tree's mask when deriving it.

TreeStore filtering is ancestor-aware (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:588-713`): a node is kept when it matches, when an ancestor matched, or when a descendant matched. `_keptNodes` holds the mask (`null` when unfiltered). A level that adopts the mask shows what a tree grid over the store shows at that depth, expansion aside.

## The Fix

- `src/data/TreeStore.mjs`: public `isKept(nodeOrKey)` answers whether the active filters keep a node (record, raw node or key, with the canonical-key fallback `get()` uses). The internal projection loops (`collectVisibleDescendants()`, `updateSiblingStats()`) keep reading the mask directly: they already hold canonical keys on a hot path.
- `src/menu/List.mjs`:
  - `syncLevelRecords()` adds only children `isKept()` keeps.
  - `onConstructed()` also subscribes to the source store's `filter` event (`onSourceStoreFilter()` re-derives the level, the shape of `onSourceStoreSort()`); `destroy()` unsubscribes it symmetrically.
  - `onSourceStoreMutate()` skips additions `isKept()` rejects.
  - When a re-derive or a removal takes away the record whose submenu is open, that submenu hides, so no floating level outlives its item.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Contract / fallback | Documentation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TreeStore.isKept(nodeOrKey)` | Existing ancestor-aware `filter()` mask and Store key resolution | Record, raw node or key → Boolean; canonical-key fallback; no active mask keeps nodes independently of expansion | New method JSDoc beside structural `getChildren()` | Real TreeStore/menu filter controls |
| `TreeStore.getChildren(parentId)` | Existing Structural Layer contract | Still returns all direct children, including filtered-out children; current sibling ordering remains the store's | Existing method JSDoc | Structural read assertion under an active filter |
| Tree-driven `Menu.List` levels | Shared source store; level-owned flat stores | Adopt the source mask on derive/filter/mutate; hide a cascade whose item leaves; detach the filter listener at destruction; classic items unchanged | Level derive, event and cleanup methods | Existing owning spec plus new filter, identity, cascade and teardown controls |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a filter set before the menu exists, every level (root and nested) lists only kept records: red on `dev`, green after.
- [ ] Changing or clearing the tree store's filters re-derives every live level, including an open submenu.
- [ ] A record added under an active filter appears in its level only when the filter keeps it.
- [ ] A filter that hides the record whose submenu is open hides that submenu.
- [ ] A destroyed level leaves no `filter` listener on the source store (extends the existing "no listener behind" test in `test/playwright/unit/menu/ListTreeStore.spec.mjs`).
- [ ] `TreeStore#getChildren()` still returns filtered-out children; its existing tests stay green.
- [ ] Classic nested-`items` menus are unchanged (existing classic test stays green).
- [ ] `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/menu test/playwright/unit/data` green.

## Out of Scope

- Changing TreeStore's ancestor-aware filter semantics.
- Filtering classic nested-`items` submenus (they are built from plain arrays, not from a store).
